tabs.scenario: Scenario Explorer – BTC Price Paths & Net Profit

scenario.heading: Scenario Explorer – BTC Price Paths & Net Profit
scenario.description: This view projects how your mining setup could perform over time under different hypothetical Bitcoin price paths. Each line stacks monthly revenue minus power costs so you can see cumulative net profit for your configuration.
howCalculatedBullets: Starts from your hashrate, power draw, electricity rate, BTC price, and upfront CAPEX.
Applies four BTC price paths: Flat (0%/yr), Conservative (20%/yr), Bullish (40%/yr), and optional Ultra (60%/yr).
For each month: revenue = BTC mined × price path; power = kW × hours × $/kWh; net = revenue − power; cumulative net sums the net month over month.
howToReadBullets: Steeper lines indicate faster payback and higher ROI.
Where a line crosses your initial CAPEX (if shown) is the estimated payback month for that scenario.
The flat path is the built-in ‘worst case’ here (no BTC appreciation, no difficulty changes).
scenario.takeaways: Takeaways: Efficient hardware plus low power can still work on flatter price paths; higher BTC growth shortens payback but isn’t guaranteed. This is a what-if tool, not a prediction.
scenario.miningVsHodlIntro: Compares two strategies using the same starting capital: buying miners and running them versus buying BTC once and holding it along the same price path.
scenario.miningVsHodlDetail: Mining value = CAPEX + cumulative net (revenue – power) using your quote inputs. HODL value uses the same starting capital to buy BTC at today’s price and revalues along the same curve.
scenario.miningVsHodlInterpretation: If the mining line stays below the HODL line, buying BTC would have outperformed under those assumptions. If mining crosses and stays above, operations would outperform in that scenario.
scenario.disclaimer: Hypothetical BTC price paths, not predictions or financial advice.

breakeven.heading: Breakeven Analysis
breakeven.description: The breakeven heatmap shows how daily net profit changes as BTC price and electricity cost vary. It highlights the BTC price needed to offset your power bill at different rates.
breakeven.formula: For each BTC price and electricity price pair we compute: revenue = dailyBtc × BTC price; electricity = totalPowerKw × 24 × $/kWh; net = revenue − electricity. Cells shade red for losses, neutral around breakeven, green for profit.
breakeven.reading: Read across the row closest to your actual power rate (e.g., $0.08/kWh) to see how net profit responds to BTC price. Where the color shifts toward neutral/green is your rough breakeven if other factors stay constant.

passive.heading: Passive Income Comparison
passive.description: This bar chart compares annual income from mining to other passive-income style investments, assuming the same $10,000 starting capital.
passive.details: Mining income uses your monthly net profit scaled to a $10k allocation. Other bars use simple, illustrative yields: dividend stocks (~3%), rentals (~5%), savings/T-bills (~4%), gold (~1%), and BTC HODL (0% income, pure price exposure).
passive.interpretation: If the mining bar is higher, your configuration implies more annual cashflow—but usually with higher operational and market risk. Some alternatives trade yield for stability or pure price exposure.
passive.disclaimer: These are hypothetical yields for comparison only; actual results and risks vary by investment and operator capability.

risk.heading: Risk & Insurance
risk.description: This section summarizes common mining risks and outlines insurance and mitigation ideas. It complements the charts by looking at downside scenarios tied to BTC price, network difficulty, power costs, and operations.
risk.checklist: Use it as a checklist to stress-test your plan: What if BTC halves in price, power rates rise, hardware fails, or regulation shifts? The mitigation bullets point to insurance, SLAs, hedging, and custody practices you can investigate with qualified professionals.

riskAndInsurance.risksIntro: Use these prompts to pressure-test the scenarios above. Each card outlines how a risk shows up in the real world and how to simulate it with the ROI explorer, tables, or heatmaps.
riskAndInsurance.stressTestLabel: How to stress-test it in this tool
riskAndInsurance.mitigationIntro: Options to investigate; not recommendations or endorsements.
riskAndInsurance.howToUse: How to use this section: combine the stress tests, tables, and charts above with these risk ideas to outline your own best-, base-, and worst-case playbooks. This content is for information only and not legal, tax, financial, or insurance advice. Work with qualified professionals before making decisions.

risks.title: Bitcoin price risk
risks.description: BTC revenue is volatile and denominated in an asset that can fall sharply just as your power bills come due in fiat.
practice: Payback can stretch out months or never arrive if BTC spends long periods below your modeled price curve.
Running costs (power, hosting, interest) stay denominated in USD, so drawdowns hit cash flow immediately.
risks.stressTest: Try dropping the BTC price curve by 30–50% in the Scenario Explorer and compare new payback months.

risks.title: Difficulty growth & halvings
risks.description: Network difficulty tends to rise with new hashrate, and halvings instantly cut the block subsidy every ~4 years.
practice: Sudden difficulty jumps reduce BTC earned per TH/s before you have time to upgrade hardware.
Halving events can cut revenue in half overnight if price does not re-rate quickly enough.
risks.stressTest: Reduce the BTC mined per month or increase operating costs to mimic a post-halving environment.

risks.title: Electricity cost & power supply
risks.description: Power contracts, grid curtailment, and seasonal demand swings can change your effective $/kWh at short notice.
practice: Unexpected tariff hikes or curtailment clauses can double operating costs or force downtime.
Demand charges and variable fuel costs can erode margins even if BTC price stays flat.
risks.stressTest: Increase the electricity input in the Scenario Explorer or breakeven heatmap to see new net margins.

risks.title: Hardware procurement & reliability
risks.description: ASICs are capital-intensive, face long lead times, and can fail without warning when run 24/7 in harsh conditions.
practice: Repair queues or shipping delays can sideline rigs for weeks, slashing daily revenue.
Next-gen models often arrive before ROI is realized, making older fleets uncompetitive.
risks.stressTest: In Scenario Explorer, lower hashrate or uptime percentages to simulate part of the fleet going offline.

risks.title: Operational, regulatory & tax
risks.description: Hosting contracts, permitting, and local policy can change faster than expected, impacting uptime or cash flows.
practice: Site-specific outages, strikes, or unfavorable regulation can halt mining even if your hardware is ready.
Import/export controls or taxes can trap capital when trying to move or sell equipment.
risks.stressTest: Model downtime or higher operating costs, and review the payback summary for new best/worst cases.

risks.title: Counterparty & custody of mined BTC
risks.description: Mining revenue often accumulates on pools, exchanges, or hosted wallets that carry theft and solvency risk.
practice: Large balances sitting on a single exchange or hot wallet increase the blast radius of a compromise.
Operational errors (lost keys, poor multi-sig discipline) can permanently destroy mined BTC.
risks.stressTest: Compare holding all mined BTC vs. selling monthly using the Mining vs. HODL table to gauge exposure.

items.name: Hardware insurance (property & inland marine)
items.description: Ask about coverage for fire, theft, transit damage, and whether hashboards are covered while installed off-site.
pros: Helps recover capex after a covered event.
Some policies include expedited repair or replacement riders.
limitations: Availability varies by jurisdiction and underwriters often require strict facility controls.
Premiums and deductibles can rival several months of profit.

items.name: Hosting facility insurance & SLAs
items.description: Request proof of property/casualty coverage, understand business interruption clauses, and document uptime guarantees.
pros: Transfers part of the facility-level risk to a party with balance sheet capacity.
limitations: Claims may require lengthy investigations and only cover specific perils.
SLAs often cap compensation and rarely repay lost BTC revenue exactly.

items.name: Business interruption / contingent coverage
items.description: Ask whether lost mining revenue or extra expense from a covered outage could be reimbursed, and what triggers payment.
pros: Provides cash to cover fixed costs while equipment is offline.
limitations: Usually tied to narrowly defined perils and capped payouts.
Documentation burden is high; small operators may not qualify.

items.name: BTC price hedging
items.description: Discuss collars, puts, or structured products that lock in a minimum USD value for future production.
pros: Stabilizes cash flow and debt service even during price drawdowns.
limitations: Premiums or margin requirements add cost.
Upside is capped if BTC rallies above the hedge strike.

items.name: Forward power contracts / fixed-price energy
items.description: Ask utilities or independent power providers about fixed-rate blocks, take-or-pay structures, or demand-response credits.
pros: Locks in a predictable operating cost for modeling payback.
May unlock cheaper financing if lenders see stable power costs.
limitations: You may owe for power even if curtailment or downtime hits.
Long-term fixed contracts can be above spot when prices fall.

items.name: Cold storage & multi-signature
items.description: Ask custodians or wallet providers about hardware security modules, segregation of client assets, and multi-sig policies.
pros: Reduces single-point-of-failure risk compared to keeping balances on exchanges.
Improves auditability for lenders or partners.
limitations: Operational overhead (signing ceremonies, key rotation) adds friction.
Losing quorum or hardware devices can delay payouts if not planned carefully.

items.name: Counterparty diversification
items.description: Keep mining pool payouts, treasury storage, and exchange accounts split across reputable providers with clear solvency reports.
pros: Limits blast radius if one venue freezes withdrawals or is hacked.
limitations: More accounts mean more operational processes and KYC reviews to maintain.
